spec_match.rationale: Compares margin-trim: block — the shipped grammar — against the four real legacy techniques on identical markup, with correctness defined by measured flushness rather than assertion.

interactive.rationale: The hide-first-child checkbox and Re-measure button re-run all five lanes, each with its CSS, live demo, measured verdict and cost note.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises four workarounds side by side 'with what each one breaks', and the page delivers the five-lane comparison including the owl-selector surprise.

edge_cases.rationale: The display:none case is the demo (verified: hiding the first child flipped :first-child AND the owl lane from ok to wrong with an accurate explanation), and the unsupported margin-trim lane is explicitly narrated as unable to demonstrate here rather than silently failing.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's rendered-box behavioural assertions (edges trimmed, sibling gaps untouched) pin the exact flushness definition this page measures.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: initial verdicts first-last:ok, owl:ok, nothing/negative/trim:wrong; after hiding the first child 0 of 5 sat flush with the owl lane reading 'gap remains — top 14px, bottom 0px' and the narration explaining the DOM-adjacency reason plus the unsupported-trim caveat; console clean, no exceptions; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each render logs and emits showcaseTelemetry.assert('workarounds-measured', …) with hideFirst, correct count and support flag.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, correct/wrong lanes recolour border plus mono verdict text, amber padding band gives the flushness a visible referent.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled checkbox with 44px hit area, per-lane text verdicts (not colour alone), aria-live summary narration.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; lanes stack to one column on mobile in the screenshot.

openQuestions.title: Show what the negative-margin lane breaks, not just that its inside gaps remain
openQuestions.detail: The negative-container-margin lane is judged by the same inside-flushness metric as the others, so it reads 'gap remains 14px' — but that technique's actual behaviour is cancelling the gap outside the container while leaving the inside measurement unchanged, and its cost note says exactly that. Adding visible neighbour elements above/below the lane demo (so the container's overlap onto them is seen and measured) would make the verdict demonstrate the note instead of talking past it.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the margin-trim lane on a supporting build
openQuestions.detail: On Chromium 141 the margin-trim lane necessarily measures like the do-nothing lane and the narration says so; one pass on Chrome 155/Canary should confirm it turns ok in both checkbox states, completing the page's argument with observed data.

summary: The best page in this feature: the owl-selector failure under display:none is reproduced live rather than claimed, and every verdict is a measured number against a visible padding band. Verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/margin-trim/the-workarounds/ — hide-first flipped both selector lanes to wrong (0/5 flush) with honest narration including the unsupported margin-trim caveat; console clean; no overflow on either device class. Feature /conformance/ route ran 0 pass / 7 fail, all honest pre-155 gaps.
